title: Weekly Scientific Lineage · 2026-W46
executive_summary:
This week’s transient chain runs from core-collapse binary assembly and neutrino energy deposition, through jet survival and CSM shock radiation, to FRB dispersion, ultrahigh-energy neutrinos, and X-ray timing diagnostics of the accretion flow.
- **Black-hole binary assembly**: arXiv:2611.08604 showed that asymmetric fallback (the Tug-boat) can raise or suppress natal kicks ($v_{\rm Tug}\sim 2$ or $\sim 0.2$) but that even $v_{\rm kick}\sim 1000\,\mathrm{km\,s^{-1}}$ does not persistently produce $\chi_{\rm eff}<0$, while eccentricities deviate from the instantaneous mass-loss approximation by up to $\sim 60\%$.
- **Neutrino engines for jets**: arXiv:2611.08742 found that equipartition flavour conversion cuts $\nu\bar\nu$ annihilation by $54\%$ in flat space but raises it by $+11\%$ in Kerr spacetime ($a=0.99$) because cross pairs are amplified by $6.3$–$7.4\times$; arXiv:2611.08595 argued that mean-field quantum kinetic equations emerge only for large $N$ ($N\gtrsim 300$ for $\nu$–$\nu$).
- **GRB jets, flares, and the MeV line**: arXiv:2611.13350 separated early–narrow ($\sim 80\%$) and late–wide ($\sim 20\%$) X-ray flare populations with distinct $L$–$t_{\rm pk}$ slopes; arXiv:2611.14363 ruled out single-scattering line-seed inverse-Compton models for the MeV feature of GRB 221009A, with compact line-photon budgets short by factors $\sim 4$–$9$; arXiv:2611.09216 found that $r$-process heating supplies only $L_{\rm EE}\sim 10^{43}$–$10^{44}\,\mathrm{erg\,s^{-1}}$ and that polar fallback chokes secondary jets unless $f_{\rm circ}\gtrsim 0.08$ for $\theta_j\le 0.3\,\mathrm{rad}$.
- **Superluminous supernovae and CSM**: arXiv:2611.10140 showed that 105 of 106 hydrogen-rich SLSNe are narrow-line SLSNe-IIn, with $\dot{M}\sim 0.028$–$0.30\,M_\odot\,\mathrm{yr^{-1}}$ and only $\sim 6\%$ Ia-CSM-like, so high luminosity plus narrow Balmer lines is not a unique core-collapse tag.
- **FRB dispersion environments**: arXiv:2611.12860 measured a foreground-halo DM excess of $119\pm 44\,\mathrm{pc\,cm^{-3}}$ ($\sim 2.6\sigma$) inside $D_L\le 50\,\mathrm{Mpc}$ and one virial radius, with a CGM-like decline in impact parameter.
- **Ultrahigh-energy neutrinos and cosmic rays**: arXiv:2611.14350 reported zero array-wide ARA events against $0.13\pm 0.01$ background and the strongest $90\%$ CL diffuse limit over $50$–$1000\,\mathrm{EeV}$; arXiv:2611.09343 argued that torus-stripped ejected nuclei let UFO shocks reach $E\gtrsim 10^{19}\,\mathrm{eV}$.
- **Compact-object X-ray timing (support wing)**: arXiv:2611.08882 favoured a wedge corona and $a>0.96$ for Cyg X-1 from jet-aligned polarization, while arXiv:2611.08769 and arXiv:2611.09635 tied QPO bicoherence ridges and hypotenuses to phase-locked multiplicative coupling rather than intrinsic nonlinearity.

overview_matrix.domain: Black-hole binary formation and natal kicks
overview_matrix.key_question: Can hydrodynamic natal kicks and asymmetric fallback flip binary orbital angular momentum enough to yield persistent $\chi_{\rm eff}<0$, and does instantaneous mass loss reproduce post-supernova orbits and merger times?
overview_matrix.core_findings:
- [arXiv:2611.08604] (hydrodynamic natal-kick study): For $E_{\rm SN}\ge 0.6 E_{\rm bin}$, Tug-boat fallback gives $v_{\rm Tug}\sim 2$ in the $28\,M_\odot$ and $34\,M_\odot$ models, while low energies suppress kicks to $v_{\rm Tug}\sim 0.2$; retro-orbital kicks $\sim 1000\,\mathrm{km\,s^{-1}}$ still do not sustain $\chi_{\rm eff}<0$. Semi-major axes match instantaneous mass loss to $\le 10\%$, but eccentricities differ by up to $\sim 60\%$, shifting $t_{\rm merge}$ through $\frac{dE}{dt}\propto M_{\rm bh1}M_{\rm bh2}M a^{-5}f(e)$.
- [arXiv:2611.09338] (hierarchical-triple GW search): The pair GW230729_082317 and GW231118_005626 has a hierarchical Bayes factor $\mathcal{B}=110$, but prior odds pull the posterior odds to $\mathcal{O}\approx 0.1$; a $1$G remnant $M_{\rm rem}\approx 19.4\,M_\odot$ overlaps the $2$G primary, with $90\%$ rate limits $R_0\in[4.2,75.3]\,\mathrm{Gpc^{-3}\,yr^{-1}}$ (null) or $[4.1,95.1]$ if confirmed ($t_{\rm max}=10\,\mathrm{yr}$).
overview_matrix.significance: Asymmetric fallback changes kick magnitude more readily than orbital orientation, so negative effective spins are not a generic hydrodynamic outcome, while eccentricity errors—not semi-major-axis errors—dominate gravitational-wave delay times. A hierarchical triple remains possible but is not yet favoured once the low prior is included.

overview_matrix.domain: Relativistic jets, GRB flares, and prompt spectral features
overview_matrix.key_question: Are X-ray flares one engine-driven sequence or two mechanisms, can line-seed inverse Compton explain the MeV feature of GRB 221009A, and can fallback power short-GRB extended emission without choking the jet?
overview_matrix.core_findings:
- [arXiv:2611.13350] (Swift X-ray flare study): A rest-frame GMM splits flares into early–narrow ($\sim 80\%$, $\langle t_{\rm pk}\rangle\simeq 10^{2}\,\mathrm{s}$, $w/t_{\rm pk}\lesssim 1$) and late–wide ($\sim 20\%$, $\langle t_{\rm pk}\rangle\simeq 10^{3.5}\,\mathrm{s}$, $w/t_{\rm pk}\gtrsim 2$). Mean flare energies agree ($\langle\log_{10} E_{\rm iso,f,rest}\rangle=51.13\pm 0.10$ vs $50.66\pm 0.20$, K–S $p=0.22$), but $L_{\rm avg}\propto t_{\rm pk}^{-1.74}$ only for the early class (late slope $-0.19^{+1.01}_{-0.93}$). Global $\beta=1.21^{+0.06}_{-0.06}$ in $\log w=\alpha+\beta\log t_{\rm pk}$ is driven by the early population.
- [arXiv:2611.14363] (GRB 221009A line-seed study): Scattering host-frame Ly$\alpha$ or H$\alpha$ to $10\,\mathrm{MeV}$ needs $\gamma_{e,{\rm Ly}\alpha}\simeq 531$ and $\gamma_{e,{\rm H}\alpha}\simeq 1.23\times 10^{3}$. No one of 40 molecular/screen combinations stays under the adopted MeV envelope; ideal line densities still fall short by $\sim 4$–$9$, and the four-interval $\gamma_0$ sequence is non-monotonic, so a falling centroid is not unique evidence of electron cooling.
- [arXiv:2611.09216] (BNS fallback study): Jet fate is set by $\widetilde L\propto f_{\rm circ}/(\xi_{\rm pol}\theta_j^2)$. For $f_{\rm npc}\simeq 0.52$ and $\theta_j\le 0.3\,\mathrm{rad}$, breakout survives when $f_{\rm circ}\gtrsim 0.08$. Diffusion-corrected $r$-process heating yields only $L_{\rm EE}\sim 10^{43}$–$10^{44}\,\mathrm{erg\,s^{-1}}$, short of observed extended emission; local temperatures $4$–$5$ times $T_{\rm eff}$ would overestimate luminosity by $\sim 10^{2}$–$10^{3}$ if used as the photosphere.
overview_matrix.significance: Flare width–time scaling is not universal, so a single viscous clock should not be fit to the whole Swift flare sample. Neither fluorescent line seeds nor pure radioactive fallback close the energy budget of the brightest MeV/extended-emission phenomenology without additional engine power and a clear polar funnel.

overview_matrix.key_question: Are luminous narrow-line SLSNe-IIn only the bright tail of SNe IIn, what pre-explosion $\dot M$ do they require, and do narrow Balmer lines plus high luminosity uniquely imply core collapse rather than Ia-CSM?
overview_matrix.core_findings: - [arXiv:2611.10140] (ZTF hydrogen-rich SLSN study): Of 106 events with peak $M\le -19.9$, 105 show narrow Balmer lines; SN 2022lvm is the only broad-lined SLSN-II in the 2021–2022 subset comparison ($1/36$). $L_{{\rm H}\alpha}$ spans $2.2\times 10^{40}$ to $1.5\times 10^{42}\,\mathrm{erg\,s^{-1}}$ (median $2.6\times 10^{41}$). The median Balmer decrement rises from $2.85$ before $+100\,\mathrm{d}$ to $4.40$ afterward, still below Ia-CSM medians $6.58$ and $17.76$. After cuts, shell speed correlates with peak magnitude ($r=0.63$, $p=0.010$). For 13 objects at $v_{\rm CSM}=100\,\mathrm{km\,s^{-1}}$ and $\epsilon=0.5$, $\dot M\sim 0.028$–$0.30\,M_\odot\,\mathrm{yr^{-1}}$ from $L=\frac{1}{2}\epsilon\dot M v_{\rm s}^3/u_{\rm w}$. About $6\%$ ($6/105$) are Ia-CSM-like, and narrow lines can persist past $+200\,\mathrm{d}$ with no Balmer morphology unique to SLSNe-IIn.
overview_matrix.significance: The luminous IIn sequence is continuous with fainter interaction supernovae and demands sustained dense hydrogen mass loss, but a non-negligible Ia-CSM contaminant means narrow lines plus $M\lesssim -20$ are not, by themselves, a core-collapse certificate.

overview_matrix.domain: Fast radio bursts and foreground halo dispersion
overview_matrix.key_question: Do foreground galaxy CGM halos imprint an extragalactic FRB DM excess whose radial trend traces CGM baryons rather than large-scale structure or host mismatch?
overview_matrix.core_findings: - [arXiv:2611.12860] (CHIME/FRB BaseCat2 halo study): Inside $D_L\le 50\,\mathrm{Mpc}$ and one virial radius the mean excess is $119\pm 44\,\mathrm{pc\,cm^{-3}}$ ($p=0.0053$, $\sim 2.6\sigma$). Across 628 intersections to $150\,\mathrm{Mpc}$, mean DM declines with impact parameter ($p=0.0046$), mainly for $10\le\log(M_*/M_\odot)\le 11$. The fit $n_e^{\rm CGM}(r)=n_{e,0}[1+(r/r_c)^2]^{-3\beta/2}$ gives $n_{e,0}=(1.7$–$21.1)\times 10^{-3}\,\mathrm{cm^{-3}}$ and $\beta=0.68^{+0.15}_{-0.16}$. The excess peaks near $\sim 90\pm 75\,\mathrm{pc\,cm^{-3}}$ at $0.2\lesssim b_{\rm min}/r_{\rm CGM}\lesssim 0.4$, while large-scale structure contributes only $\sim 14\pm 39\,\mathrm{pc\,cm^{-3}}$.
overview_matrix.significance: A CGM-scale DM term is tentatively detected and is radially structured, so host- and IGM-only DM budgets will misassign baryons for sightlines that pierce nearby halos; the significance is still only $\sim 2.6\sigma$ and must be read as a constraint, not a completed CGM census.

overview_matrix.domain: Ultrahigh-energy neutrinos, cosmic rays, and dense multi-messenger sites
overview_matrix.key_question: What diffuse flux of $E_\nu\gtrsim 10^{17}\,\mathrm{eV}$ neutrinos is allowed, and can shocks around ejected galactic nuclei accelerate protons to $E\ge 10^{19}\,\mathrm{eV}$ once the dusty torus is removed?
overview_matrix.core_findings:
- [arXiv:2611.14350] (ARA array-wide search): Over $28$ station-years ($10.6$ array-equivalent years after cuts), $n=0$ events are seen against $0.13\pm 0.01\,{\rm (stat.)}^{+0.05}_{-0.06}\,{\rm (syst.)}$ background. The Feldman–Cousins $90\%$ CL limit is the strongest in $50$–$1000\,\mathrm{EeV}$. Expected counts exclude a global upper-limit model at $\mu=5.3$ ($2.6\sigma$, $99\%$) and a Muzio model at $\mu=2.4$ ($1.3\sigma$, $90\%$), while a KM3NeT-motivated flux ($\mu=1.6$) is only $77\%$ excluded. Low-energy systematics are $\sim 50\%$ (Askaryan model) and high-energy systematics $\sim 150\%$ (cross section).
- [arXiv:2611.09343] (ejected-nuclei cosmic-ray study): UFO shocks in torus-stripped, expanding nuclei reach $E\gtrsim 10^{19}\,\mathrm{eV}$ at $r\sim 2$–$3\,\mathrm{pc}$, about an order of magnitude above the $10^{17}$–$10^{18}\,\mathrm{eV}$ ceiling of stationary, torus-embedded nuclei, using $\dot E\sim 0.05 L_{\rm bol}$, $\xi_B\sim 0.1$, and Bohm-limited $E_{\rm max}\propto \xi_B^{1/2}\rho^{-1/6}\dot E^{2/3}r^{-1/3}$.
overview_matrix.significance: Radio-array exposure is now excluding the brighter cosmogenic and source-stacked UHE neutrino models near $0.05$–$1\,\mathrm{ZeV}$, while photohadronic losses—not the shock itself—set the UHECR ceiling, so ejecting the nucleus from its torus is a geometrically specific way to raise $E_{\rm max}$.

overview_matrix.domain: Compact-binary gravitational waves and neutron-star tides
overview_matrix.key_question: Can Newtonian SPH recover the finite-size tidal contribution to binary neutron-star gravitational waves without full numerical relativity?
overview_matrix.core_findings: - [arXiv:2611.08642] (PHANTOM tidal-strain study): With $\sim 10^{4}$ SPH particles, rescaling the Newtonian tidal strain by $\xi_{{\rm N}\to{\rm GR}}=k_2^{\rm GR}/k_2^{\rm N}\simeq 0.200$ ($k_2^{\rm N}=0.2599$, $k_2^{\rm GR}=0.0520$) gives $\Delta h_{\rm SPH}^{\rm tide,GR}\simeq\xi_{{\rm N}\to{\rm GR}}\Delta h_{\rm SPH}^{\rm tide,N}$, matching the NR-calibrated Rising Tides model at separations $60$–$80\,\mathrm{km}$.
overview_matrix.significance: A Love-number rescaling lets inexpensive SPH isolate the tidal excess in the late inspiral, but the calibration is validated only outside the last few orbits and does not replace numerical relativity for merger waveforms.

overview_matrix.domain: Black-hole and white-dwarf X-ray binaries: polarization, QPOs, and accretion geometry
overview_matrix.key_question: Can energy-dependent polarization and bispectral phase coupling break the lamppost-versus-extended-corona degeneracy and separate geometric precession from radiative modulation?
overview_matrix.core_findings:
- [arXiv:2611.08882] (KerrC polarization study): In the low-hard state of Cyg X-1, a radially extended wedge matches the $\sim 4\%$ (IXPE) and $\sim 5\%$ (XL-Calibur) polarization parallel to the radio jet better than a lamppost. In the soft state, $\sim 2\%$ jet-parallel polarization from returning radiation requires $a>0.96$.
- [arXiv:2611.08769] (QPO bicoherence model): Cross-arm, hypotenuse, and harmonic-point patterns follow from bilinear and quadratic coupling of a QPO to log-normal flow noise, with $b^2_{\rm point}=\tau^2\tau_2/(2-\tau^2)$ independent of the noise amplitude.
- [arXiv:2611.09635] (multiplicative QPO modulation study): In the weak-modulation limit, $|B_{\rm ridge}|\simeq (u_1 a_1/4) P(\nu)$ with $\phi_{\rm bi}^{\rm ridge}\simeq -\Delta_1$, while the hypotenuse has the opposite biphase. NICER data for Swift J1727.8$-$1613 and MAXI J1820$+$070 show $\sim +\pi/2$ on the fundamental ridge and between $-\pi/2$ and $-\pi$ on the hypotenuse.
- [arXiv:2611.09556] (AR UMa XMM-Newton study): The $B\approx 160\,\mathrm{MG}$ polar is dominated by a $kT_{\rm bb}=35\pm 0.53\,\mathrm{eV}$ blackbody with $F_{\rm bb}/F_{\rm plasma}>500$ and $\dot M\approx (1.2$–$1.9)\times 10^{-10}\,M_\odot\,\mathrm{yr^{-1}}$, so a steady shock with $L_{\rm reprocessed}/L_{\rm shock}\approx 0.5$ does not describe the high state.
overview_matrix.significance: Polarization selects an extended hard-state corona and a near-extremal soft-state spin, while biphase sign reversal is the observable of multiplicative QPO–noise coupling. Extreme polars show that buried, blobby accretion can erase the hard shock component that steady models assume.

thematic_highlights.theme_name: Engines: kicks, neutrinos, and jet survival
thematic_highlights.summary: Binary assembly and jet launching are both limited by how mass and neutrinos are redistributed after collapse. arXiv:2611.08604 finds that fallback asymmetry rescales kick speed ($v_{\rm Tug}$ from $\sim 0.2$ to $\sim 2$) without reliably reversing orbital orientation, and that a $\sim 60\%$ eccentricity error, not the $\le 10\%$ semi-major-axis error, dominates the Peters merger-time shift. arXiv:2611.08742 shows the opposite of a universal flavour penalty: Kerr lensing and frame dragging raise cross-pair annihilation enough that equipartition conversion increases energy deposition by $+11\%$ even though the same conversion suppresses flat-space deposition by $54\%$, with $50\%$ of $\dot E_\infty$ inside $r<10M$. Downstream, arXiv:2611.09216 shows polar quasi-spherical fallback is both fuel and obstacle: $\widetilde L\propto f_{\rm circ}/(\xi_{\rm pol}\theta_j^2)$ leaves $\theta_j\le 0.3$ jets unchoked only for $f_{\rm circ}\gtrsim 0.08$, and diffusion-corrected $r$-process power ($10^{43}$–$10^{44}\,\mathrm{erg\,s^{-1}}$) cannot replace that engine for short-GRB extended emission.

thematic_highlights.theme_name: GRB radiation: two flare clocks and a failed MeV line seed
thematic_highlights.summary: Prompt and early afterglow variability do not share one temporal law. arXiv:2611.13350 isolates an early–narrow flare majority ($\sim 80\%$, $w/t_{\rm pk}\sim 0.76$, $L\propto t_{\rm pk}^{-1.74}$) from a late–wide minority ($w/t_{\rm pk}\sim 2$, slope consistent with zero) whose isotropic energies nevertheless match, arguing against reading the combined $L_{\rm pk}\propto t_{\rm pk}^{-3}$ trend as a single accretion index. arXiv:2611.14363 closes a specific radiation channel for GRB 221009A: H$_2$ fluorescence, hydrogen recombination, and metal K-shell seeds, scattered once, cannot jointly meet photon supply, the LAT continuum, and escape. Required Lorentz factors are $\gamma_e\sim 5\times 10^{2}$–$10^{3}$ for eV seeds at $10\,\mathrm{MeV}$, trial UV centroids sit at $\sim 161$–$210\,\mathrm{MeV}$, and even ideal excitation underproduces the line density by $\sim 4$–$9$. A non-monotonic $\gamma_0$ across four time bins further warns against equating a drifting centroid with monotonic cooling.

arXiv:2611.10140 places hydrogen-rich SLSNe on the IIn sequence rather than in a separate spectroscopic class: 105/106 events have narrow Balmer emission, median $L_{{\rm H}\alpha}=2.6\times 10^{41}\,\mathrm{erg\,s^{-1}}$, and shock-powered mass-loss rates $0.028$–$0.30\,M_\odot\,\mathrm{yr^{-1}}$ at the adopted $v_{\rm CSM}=100\,\mathrm{km\,s^{-1}}$ and $\epsilon=0.5$. Brighter peaks tend to have slower shells ($r=0.63$). The Balmer decrement increases after $+100\,\mathrm{d}$ but stays well below Ia-CSM comparison samples, and the $\sim 6\%$ Ia-CSM-like fraction is the practical contaminant for engine-versus-interaction classifications. No line-profile feature separates these SLSNe-IIn from fainter SNe IIn, including interaction that lasts beyond $+200\,\mathrm{d}$.

thematic_highlights.theme_name: Multi-messenger backgrounds: FRB DM, UHE neutrinos, and UHECRs
thematic_highlights.summary: Propagation screens and source geometry both moved from assumptions to limits. arXiv:2611.12860 finds a $119\pm 44\,\mathrm{pc\,cm^{-3}}$ DM excess on nearby halo sightlines and a declining trend with $b_{\rm min}/r_{\rm CGM}$, with large-scale structure contributing only $\sim 14\pm 39\,\mathrm{pc\,cm^{-3}}$; the implied CGM index is $\beta\approx 0.68$. arXiv:2611.14350 converts a null ARA search into the leading $50$–$1000\,\mathrm{EeV}$ diffuse limit, excluding the brightest benchmark at $99\%$ while leaving a KM3NeT-like flux only mildly constrained ($\mu=1.6$, $77\%$). arXiv:2611.09343 complements that by showing stationary tori cap protons near $10^{17}$–$10^{18}\,\mathrm{eV}$, whereas ejected nuclei can reach $\gtrsim 10^{19}\,\mathrm{eV}$ at a few parsecs. arXiv:2611.09037 adds that flavour-dependent dark-matter potentials can distort IceCube flavour ratios enough to turn an upper limit into a lower limit if only $V_\mu$ is large.

thematic_highlights.theme_name: Accretion-flow geometry from polarization and bispectra
thematic_highlights.summary: Second-order PSDs do not identify the corona or the QPO coupling. arXiv:2611.08882 uses IXPE and XL-Calibur polarization parallel to the Cyg X-1 jet to prefer a wedge over a lamppost in the hard state and returning-radiation reflection with $a>0.96$ in the soft state. arXiv:2611.08769 and arXiv:2611.09635 give a consistent bispectral picture: ridges and hypotenuses are sidebands of a phase-locked modulator, with an exact biphase reversal $\phi_{\rm bi}^{\rm ridge}\simeq -\phi_{\rm bi}^{\rm hypot}$ that NICER confirms in Swift J1727.8$-$1613 and MAXI J1820$+$070. Separately, arXiv:2611.09556 shows AR UMa’s high state is soft-blobby, with $F_{\rm bb}/F_{\rm plasma}>500$, so the canonical reprocessed-to-shock ratio $\approx 0.5$ is not universal even for magnetic accretion.

top_picks.title: Hydrodynamic Natal Kicks and Formation of Black Hole Binaries
top_picks.recommendation_reason: Directly tests whether core-collapse hydrodynamics can generate the negative effective spins used to separate dynamical and isolated binary channels.
top_picks.core_insight: Tug-boat fallback changes $v_{\rm kick}$ by factors of order two, but does not flip orbits into persistent $\chi_{\rm eff}<0$, and eccentricity errors up to $\sim 60\%$ dominate merger-time shifts.
top_picks.reading_guide: Start with the $v_{\rm Tug}(E_{\rm SN}/E_{\rm bin})$ tracks for the $28$ and $34\,M_\odot$ progenitors, then the IML comparison of $a$ versus $e$.

top_picks.title: Neutrino pair annihilation in curved spacetime: a fast moment method and the geometry of flavour conversion
top_picks.recommendation_reason: Quantifies whether neutrino annihilation can power GRB jets once gravitational ray bending and flavour mixing are treated together.
top_picks.core_insight: Equipartition flavour conversion suppresses annihilation by $54\%$ in flat space but enhances it by $+11\%$ at $a=0.99$ because cross pairs, amplified $6.3$–$7.4\times$, dominate the Kerr deposition.
top_picks.reading_guide: Read the flat-versus-Kerr pair decomposition (inner, outer, cross) before the separability-limit ratio $\mathcal{R}=0.159$.

top_picks.title: Probing circumstellar interaction with spectroscopy of ZTF hydrogen-rich superluminous supernovae
top_picks.recommendation_reason: Provides the spectroscopic mass-loss baseline for deciding when SLSNe are CSM-powered rather than engine-powered.
top_picks.core_insight: Nearly all hydrogen-rich SLSNe are SLSNe-IIn requiring $\dot{M}\sim 0.03$–$0.3\,M_\odot\,\mathrm{yr^{-1}}$, yet $\sim 6\%$ look like Ia-CSM and no Balmer morphology is unique to the luminous end.
top_picks.reading_guide: Use the Balmer-decrement and $v_{\rm s}$–magnitude correlation sections, then the $\epsilon=0.5$ mass-loss table.

top_picks.title: Search for a Dispersion Measure Excess Toward Nearby Galaxy Halos Using Fast Radio Bursts from the Second CHIME/FRB Baseband Catalog
top_picks.recommendation_reason: A concrete CGM DM term changes how FRB dispersion is partitioned among host, halo, and cosmic baryons.
top_picks.core_insight: Nearby halo crossings show a $119\pm 44\,\mathrm{pc\,cm^{-3}}$ excess ($\sim 2.6\sigma$) that declines with impact parameter and exceeds the large-scale-structure contribution.
top_picks.reading_guide: Focus on the $D_L\le 50\,\mathrm{Mpc}$ stack and the $\beta$ fit, and treat the detection as tentative.

top_picks.title: Early--Narrow and Late--Wide Populations of GRB X-ray Flares
top_picks.recommendation_reason: Challenges the single $w\propto t$ and single $L\propto t^{-3}$ descriptions used to argue that all X-ray flares share one central-engine clock.
top_picks.core_insight: About $80\%$ of flares are early and narrow with $L\propto t_{\rm pk}^{-1.74}$, while $\sim 20\%$ are late and wide with a slope consistent with zero, at statistically identical flare energies.
top_picks.reading_guide: Read the GMM centers in the $(t_{\rm pk},w)$ plane and the separate Bayesian $L$–$t$ slopes before the global $\beta=1.21$ fit.

top_picks.title: New Constraints on the Ultrahigh Energy Neutrino Flux from the First Array-Wide Search with the Askaryan Radio Array
top_picks.recommendation_reason: Sets the current benchmark diffuse limit in the $50$–$1000\,\mathrm{EeV}$ window relevant to UHECR source models and the KM3NeT candidate.
top_picks.core_insight: A null result ($n=0$ versus $0.13$ expected background) excludes the brightest global model at $99\%$ and is only weakly in tension with a KM3NeT-like flux ($\mu=1.6$).
top_picks.reading_guide: Compare the model $\mu$ table with the stated $50\%$ and $150\%$ systematics before quoting the Feldman–Cousins curve.

top_picks.title: Spectral Constraints on Line-Seed Inverse-Compton Models for the MeV Feature in GRB 221009A
top_picks.recommendation_reason: Closes a widely discussed radiation channel for the brightest GRB MeV feature using photon supply, LAT continuity, and timing together.
top_picks.core_insight: No H$_2$, hydrogen, or metal line seed survives single-scattering inverse Compton: densities are short by $\sim 4$–$9$, and the calibrated $\gamma_0$ sequence is non-monotonic.
top_picks.reading_guide: Start from the Thomson mapping $\epsilon^{\rm IC}_{\rm obs}\simeq 2\gamma_e^2\epsilon(1-\beta_e\mu_i)/(1+z)$ and then the 40-template envelope test.

top_picks.title: Quasi-spherical fallback in binary neutron-star mergers: fuel and obstacle for extended emission
top_picks.recommendation_reason: Links kilonova ejecta, secondary-jet breakout, and the energy source of short-GRB extended emission in one dynamical criterion.
top_picks.core_insight: Radioactive heating underproduces extended emission by orders of magnitude after photon diffusion, and jets with $\theta_j\le 0.3$ avoid choking only if $f_{\rm circ}\gtrsim 0.08$.
top_picks.reading_guide: Use the $\widetilde L$ regime diagram and the $T_{\rm local}/T_{\rm eff}$ luminosity correction.

top_picks.title: Modeling of the X-ray Flux and Polarization Energy Spectra of Black Hole X-Ray Binaries with the KerrC Code
top_picks.recommendation_reason: Shows how IXPE polarization breaks coronal-geometry degeneracies that flux spectra alone leave open, which matters for jet-base models.
top_picks.core_insight: Hard-state polarization parallel to the jet favours a wedge corona, while soft-state returning radiation requires $a>0.96$.
top_picks.reading_guide: Compare the lamppost and wedge polarization spectra in the $2$–$8\,\mathrm{keV}$ band before the spin posterior.

top_picks.title: GW230729_082317 and GW231118_005626: A Candidate of Hierarchical Triple Mergers
top_picks.recommendation_reason: A concrete hierarchical-merger candidate with an explicit prior-odds correction, relevant to dense-cluster channels.
top_picks.core_insight: The likelihood ratio $\mathcal{B}=110$ is real, but the posterior odds fall to $\mathcal{O}\approx 0.1$, so the pair is not yet evidence of a sequential triple.

papers.title: Hydrodynamic Natal Kicks and Formation of Black Hole Binaries
papers.result: Asymmetric fallback accretion drives the Tug-boat mechanism, where high explosion energies ($E_{\rm SN} \ge 0.6 E_{\rm bin}$) amplify final kick velocities above symmetric expectations ($v_{\rm Tug} \equiv v_f / v_{\rm sym} > 1$, reaching $v_{\rm Tug} \sim 2$ for $28\,M_\odot$ and $34\,M_\odot$), while low energies suppress kicks ($v_{\rm Tug} \sim 0.2$). Even extreme retro-orbital kicks with $v_{\rm kick} \sim 1000\ \mathrm{km\ s^{-1}}$ cannot consistently flip orbital orientation or produce persistent negative $\chi_{\rm eff}$. Although post-SN semi-major axes match Instantaneous Mass Loss (IML) calculations within $\le 10\%$, orbital eccentricities deviate by up to $\sim 60\%$, strongly shifting gravitational-wave merger timescales governed by $\frac{dE}{dt} = -\frac{32G^4}{5c^5}\frac{M_{\rm bh1}M_{\rm bh2}M}{a^5}f(e)$.
papers.problem: Whether hydrodynamic natal kicks and asymmetric fallback accretion in core-collapse supernovae can tilt binary black hole orbital angular momentum sufficiently to generate negative effective inspiral spin parameters $\chi_{\rm eff} < 0$, and whether the Instantaneous Mass Loss (IML) approximation accurately reproduces post-explosion binary orbital parameters and coalescence times.
papers.method: Performed 3D SPH hydrodynamic simulations with modified GADGET using stripped helium star progenitor models ($13\,M_\odot, 21\,M_\odot, 28\,M_\odot, 34\,M_\odot$), where central core collapse forms a sink particle with initial mass $M_{\rm bh,2,i} = 3\,M_\odot$ and initial spin $S_{\rm BH} = 0$, accreting SPH particles satisfying $r < r_{\rm acc} = 0.01\,R_\odot$ and $j < j_{\rm isco}$; asymmetric explosion energy $E_{\rm SN}/E_{\rm bin} \in [0.2, 0.9]$ is injected according to the angular profile $f(\theta,\Delta,\sigma) = 1 + \Delta e^{-\theta^2/2\sigma^2}$.
papers.reason: This study performs 3D SPH simulations to investigate the hydrodynamic Tug-boat mechanism and black hole natal kicks in core-collapse supernovae, providing critical physical limits on whether natal kicks can tilt binary orbits to produce negative effective inspiral spins $\chi_{\rm eff} < 0$.

papers.title: Neutrino pair annihilation in curved spacetime: a fast moment method and the geometry of flavour conversion
papers.result: In Kerr spacetime with spin $a = 0.99$, $T_x = T_e$, and $T_{\bar{e}} = 1.5 T_e$, equipartition flavour conversion reduces annihilation energy deposition by $54\%$ in flat spacetime but increases it by $+11\%$ in Kerr spacetime. This sign reversal is driven by cross pairs between the inner ring and outer disc: general relativity amplifies outer-outer pairs by a factor of $2.0$, but amplifies cross pairs by $6.3\text{--}7.4\times$, elevating cross pairs to $0.77$ of the total Kerr deposition (compared to $0.23$ in flat spacetime). In the exact separability limit ($f_{\nu_x} = f_{\bar{\nu}_x} = 0$), the ratio is $\mathcal{R} = (1-P)(1-\bar{P}) + \frac{D_x}{2D_e} P \bar{P} = 0.159$ at $P = \bar{P} = 2/3$ (a $6.3\times$ suppression). Gravitational redistribution concentrates energy deposition: $50\%$ of $\dot{E}_{\infty}$ originates from $r < 10M$, $90\%$ from $r < 20M$, and $73\%$ within $5M$ above the disc plane.
papers.problem: Whether neutrino pair annihilation $\nu\bar{\nu} \to e^+ e^-$ in curved spacetime can deposit sufficient energy to power relativistic jets in gamma-ray bursts, and whether general relativistic transport effects (gravitational redshift, ray bending, and frame dragging) and neutrino flavour conversion can be decoupled when electron and heavy-lepton neutrinospheres are spatially segregated.
papers.method: Exact angular moment factorisation decomposing the local energy deposition rate $\dot{q} = \frac{D G_F^2}{3\pi c^5} [\mathcal{M}(\mathcal{E}_4, \bar{\mathcal{E}}_3) + \mathcal{M}(\mathcal{E}_3, \bar{\mathcal{E}}_4)]$ and momentum deposition rate $c\dot{p}_i = \frac{D G_F^2}{3\pi c^5} [\mathcal{P}_i(\mathcal{E}_4, \bar{\mathcal{E}}_3) + \mathcal{P}_i(\bar{\mathcal{E}}_4, \mathcal{E}_3)]$ into 20 direction moments (ranks 0 to 3, with 16 independent) defined by $\mathcal{E}_n(\boldsymbol{\Omega}) = \int_0^\infty f \varepsilon^n \mathrm{d}\varepsilon$, coupled to the open-source code ANNIHILUS utilizing OpenMP C backward ray tracing with 4th-order Runge-Kutta in Mino time and edge-adapted quadrature.
papers.reason: This work establishes an exact angular moment framework for neutrino pair annihilation around black hole accretion discs and uncovers a fundamental general relativistic sign-reversal effect on flavour conversion, directly relevant to compact object central engines and relativistic jet launching in GRBs.

papers.result: Tidal excess is reliably extracted using $\sim 10^4$ SPH particles by rescaling the Newtonian tidal strain with the Love-number ratio $\xi_{\mathrm{N}\to\mathrm{GR}} = k_2^{\mathrm{GR}}/k_2^{\mathrm{N}} \simeq 0.200$ (where $k_2^{\mathrm{N}}=0.2599$ and $k_2^{\mathrm{GR}}=0.0520$), giving $\Delta h_{\mathrm{SPH}}^{\mathrm{tide,GR}}(r) \simeq \xi_{\mathrm{N}\to\mathrm{GR}}\Delta h_{\mathrm{SPH}}^{\mathrm{tide,N}}(r)$ in good agreement with the NR-calibrated Rising Tides model at separations of $60\text{--}80\,\mathrm{km}$.
papers.problem: Extracting finite-size tidal contributions to gravitational wave emission in binary neutron star coalescences without losing the signal in numerical noise or incurring the high computational cost of full numerical relativity.
papers.method: Combines Newtonian SPH simulations using \texttt{PHANTOM} with hydrostatic/hydrodynamic relaxation (HPR) to prepare quasi-equilibrium configurations, calculating the face-on gravitational strain from the second time derivative of the traceless quadrupole moment $h_{ij}^{\mathrm{TT}}(t;D)=\frac{2G}{c^4 D}\Lambda_{ij,kl}\ddot{Q}_{kl}^{\mathrm{sys}}(t)$.
papers.reason: This study demonstrates how Newtonian SPH simulations with Love-number rescaling can rapidly capture tidal excess in binary neutron star gravitational waveforms, offering a computationally efficient tool for multi-messenger transient early warnings.

papers.title: Modeling of the X-ray Flux and Polarization Energy Spectra of Black Hole X-Ray Binaries with the KerrC Code
papers.result: In the low-hard state of Cygnus X-1, modeling reproduces the observed $2\text{--}8\ \mathrm{keV}$ polarization degree of $\sim 4\%$ (IXPE) and $\sim 5\%$ (XL-Calibur) aligned parallel to the radio jet, favoring a radially extended wedge-like corona over a lamppost geometry. papers.problem: Disentangling the degenerate coronal geometries (e.g., lamppost versus slab/wedge) and constraining black hole spin in black hole X-ray binaries using energy-dependent linear polarization and flux spectra.
papers.method: Forward Monte Carlo ray tracing in Boyer-Lindquist coordinates with the xTrack code, integrating null geodesics with conserved energy $E_\gamma = -k_t$ and angular momentum $\mathcal{L}_\gamma = k_\phi$, parallel transporting polarization four-vectors via $\frac{d f^\mu}{d \lambda'} = -\Gamma^\mu_{\sigma\nu} f^\sigma k^\nu / E_\gamma$ under constraints $k^2 = 0$, $k \cdot f = 0$, $f^2 = 1$, and evaluating Compton scattering with the relativistic Fano matrix $[I_1, Q_1, U_1]^T = \mathbf{T}_{\mathrm{F}} [I_0, Q_0, U_0]^T$ across Maxwell-Jüttner electrons.
papers.reason: This work develops the kerrC spectro-polarimetric ray-tracing framework to interpret IXPE and XL-Calibur observations of black hole X-ray binaries, providing critical methodology to constrain corona geometry and black hole spin in compact object systems.

papers.title: Probing flavor-dependent neutrino-dark matter interactions with the flavor composition of high-energy cosmic neutrinos
papers.result: For $E = 100\ \mathrm{TeV}$ neutrinos from TXS 0506+056 with dark matter column density $X_\chi = 3.6 \times 10^{28}\ \mathrm{GeV/cm^2}$, the MSW potential threshold is $A_\alpha \sim 10^{-38}\ \mathrm{cm^3}(100\ \mathrm{TeV}/E)$. In the vacuum-like regime ($A_\alpha \lesssim 10^{-40}\ \mathrm{cm^3}$), IceCube flavor constraints yield $\sigma_{\nu\chi}/m_\chi \lesssim 10^{-29}\ \mathrm{cm^2/GeV}$, whereas for $V_\mu$-only interaction with $A_\mu > 9.52 \times 10^{-39}\ \mathrm{cm^3}$, the IceCube 95% C.L. constraint inverts to a lower bound requiring sufficient attenuation to prevent unacceptable flavor distortion.
papers.problem: How flavor-dependent neutrino-dark matter forward scattering and incoherent attenuation in supermassive black hole dark matter spikes distort the flavor ratio of high-energy astrophysical neutrinos relative to IceCube observations.
papers.method: The authors model neutrino propagation via the effective Hamiltonian $\mathcal{H} = \frac{1}{2E} U \mathcal{M}^2 U^\dagger + V(r) = \frac{1}{2E} U_m \mathcal{M}_m^2 U_m^\dagger$ with potential $V_\alpha(r) = A_\alpha \rho_\chi(r)$, evaluating adiabatic propagation where source mass eigenstate fluxes $F_i = \sum_\alpha |(U_m^S)_{\alpha i}|^2 f_\alpha^S$ yield Earth flavor fluxes $f_\beta^\oplus = \sum_i |(U_m^\oplus)_{\beta i}|^2 F_i$.
papers.reason: This paper investigates the flavor composition of high-energy cosmic neutrinos from blazar TXS 0506+056 under flavor-dependent neutrino-dark matter interactions, providing physical constraints testable by IceCube flavor measurements.

papers.title: Quasi-spherical fallback in binary neutron-star mergers: fuel and obstacle for extended emission
papers.result: The fate of the secondary jet is governed by the dimensionless luminosity $\widetilde{L} \propto f_{\rm circ}/(\xi_{\rm pol}\theta_{j}^{2})$, defining jet-dominated, cocoon-dominated, and choked breakout regimes. For non-promptly captured fallback fraction $f_{\rm npc} \simeq 0.52$ and circularization fractions $f_{\rm circ} \in [0.052, 0.52]$, jets with $\theta_j \le 0.3\ \mathrm{rad}$ avoid being choked when $f_{\rm circ} \gtrsim 0.08$. Furthermore, radioactive $r$-process heating has local temperature $T_{\rm local} \approx (4\text{--}5)T_{\rm eff}$, overestimating luminosity by $(T_{\rm local}/T_{\rm eff})^4 \sim 10^2\text{--}10^3$; accounting for optical diffusion, nuclear heating yields only $L_{\rm EE} \sim 10^{43}\text{--}10^{44}\ \mathrm{erg\,s^{-1}}$, insufficient to power observed short GRB extended emission.
papers.problem: Whether quasi-spherical fallback accretion in binary neutron star mergers can provide sufficient fuel to power observed short GRB extended emission without choking the secondary relativistic jet in the refilled polar ejecta, and whether pure $r$-process radioactive heating can account for extended emission energetics.
papers.method: A semi-analytic dynamical model coupled to GRMHD post-processing: fallback accretion follows $\dot{M}_{\rm FB}(t) = \dot{M}_0 t^{-5/3}$, driving secondary jet power $L_j(t) = \eta_j \dot{M}_{\rm circ}(t)c^2 = \eta_j f_{\rm circ}\dot{M}_{\rm FB}(t)c^2$ with $\eta_j = 0.1$. The polar ambient density is $\rho_{\rm pol}(r,t) = \xi_{\rm pol}\rho_{\rm FB}(r,t)$, yielding dimensionless luminosity $\widetilde{L}(t,r_h) = \frac{L_j(t)}{\Sigma_j(r_h)\rho_{\rm pol}(r_h,t)c^3} \propto \frac{f_{\rm circ}}{\xi_{\rm pol}\theta_j^2}$ and head velocity $\beta_h = \frac{1 + \widetilde{L}^{-1/2}\beta_a}{1 + \widetilde{L}^{-1/2}}$, with equivalent isotropic X-ray energy computed via $E_{X,\rm iso}^{\rm NT} = \frac{\eta_X}{f_j}\int L_j(t)\,dt$.
papers.reason: This paper investigates whether quasi-spherical fallback in binary neutron star mergers can power secondary relativistic jets for extended emission while simultaneously choking them, directly addressing central engines, relativistic jets, and breakout physics.

papers.title: GW230729\_082317 and GW231118\_005626: A Candidate of Hierarchical Triple Mergers
papers.result: For candidate pair GW230729_082317 and GW231118_005626, joint Bayesian parameter estimation yields a Bayes factor $\mathcal{B} = 110$ favoring the hierarchical triple merger hypothesis, but accounting for low prior probability reduces the posterior odds ratio to $\mathcal{O} \approx 0.1$. The 1G remnant mass ($M_{\rm rem} \approx 19.4\,M_\odot$) matches the 2G primary mass ($m_1 \sim 2m_2$) with overlapping sky localization and distance ($d_L \sim 1630\,\mathrm{Mpc}$). Under a Poisson process with delay distribution $P(\Delta < T) \propto (T/t_{\rm max})^\alpha$, the $90\%$ upper limit on the local event rate density is $R_0 \in [4.2, 75.3]\,\mathrm{Gpc^{-3}\,yr^{-1}}$ for null detection, and $R_0 \in [4.1, 95.1]\,\mathrm{Gpc^{-3}\,yr^{-1}}$ ($t_{\rm max} = 10\,\mathrm{yr}$) if confirmed.
papers.problem: Whether the paired gravitational-wave events GW230729_082317 and GW231118_005626 originate from a sequential hierarchical triple black hole merger, and how dynamical signatures in dense stellar systems constrain their formation channels.
papers.method: Searched for orbital eccentricity with SEOBNRv5EHM and line-of-sight acceleration via 3.5 PN phase corrections $\Psi(f) = \Psi_0(f) + \Delta\Psi(f)$ on GW230729_082317. Evaluated the hypothesis Bayes factor $\mathcal{O}_{\mathcal{H}_N}^{\mathcal{H}_H} = \frac{p(d_1,d_2|\mathcal{H}_H)}{p(d_1,d_2|\mathcal{H}_N)} = 110$ via joint Bayesian analysis. Analyzed dynamical interactions via critical velocity $v_{\rm c,bin-sin}^2 = \frac{Gm_1m_2(m_1+m_2+m_3)}{a_0m_3(m_1+m_2)}$ and parabolic encounter energy loss $\Delta E_{\rm parabolic}$, and inferred event rate densities $R(z) = R_0(1+z)^\kappa$.
papers.reason: The paper investigates the first observational candidate for a hierarchical triple black hole merger pair (GW230729_082317 and GW231118_005626) in LVK O4a, providing valuable empirical constraints on compact object mergers and dynamical assembly in dense environments.

papers.title: Activity of the ejected galactic nuclei and cosmic rays
papers.result: Ejected galactic nuclei stripped of their dusty tori expand into lower-density interstellar environments, allowing UFO shocks to accelerate protons up to $E \gtrsim 10^{19}\,\mathrm{eV}$ at $r \sim 2\text{--}3\,\mathrm{pc}$, which is an order of magnitude higher than the $E \sim 10^{17}\text{--}10^{18}\,\mathrm{eV}$ limit in standard stationary galactic nuclei.
papers.problem: Investigating whether cosmic ray protons accelerated in ultrafast outflow (UFO) shocks can reach ultra-high energies ($E \geq 10^{19}\,\mathrm{eV}$) when escaping the severe photohadronic radiation losses imposed by accretion disks and dusty tori in stationary galactic centers.
papers.method: Theoretical modeling of UFO shock dynamics using Dokuchaev generalized Sedov self-similar expansion $r(t) \propto (\dot{E} t^3 / \rho)^{1/5}$ with kinetic luminosity $\dot{E} = f_{\rm kin} L_{\rm bol} \sim 0.05 L_{\rm bol}$, magnetic field equipartition $B \simeq \sqrt{6\xi_B}\rho^{1/6}\dot{E}^{1/3}r^{-2/3}$ with $\xi_B \sim 0.1$, and first-order Fermi diffusive acceleration under Bohm diffusion yielding $E_{\rm max} = e B v_{\rm s}^2 t / c \propto \xi_B^{1/2} \rho^{-1/6} \dot{E}^{2/3} r^{-1/3}$.
papers.reason: The paper investigates UHECR acceleration in shocks driven by ultrafast outflows (UFOs) from ejected supermassive black holes, providing quantitative scaling relations for particle acceleration and photo-hadronic losses directly relevant to high-energy outflows and compact object environments.

papers.title: XMM-Newton observations of the highest field polar AR UMa: An extreme case of soft-blobby accretion
papers.result: AR UMa exhibits extreme soft-blobby accretion onto its southern pole ($B \approx 160\,\mathrm{MG}$, $\beta \simeq 142^\circ$) with emission dominated by a soft blackbody of $kT_{\rm bb} = 35 \pm 0.53\,\mathrm{eV}$ and bolometric flux $F_{\rm bb,bol} \approx (6.16\text{--}7.41) \times 10^{-10}\,\mathrm{erg\ s^{-1}\ cm^{-2}}$, yielding $F_{\rm bb}/F_{\rm plasma} > 500$ ($L_{\rm bb} \approx (3.95\text{--}6.39) \times 10^{32}\,\mathrm{erg\ s^{-1}}$ versus $L_{\rm plasma} \approx 1.4 \times 10^{30}\,\mathrm{erg\ s^{-1}}$) and mass accretion rate $\dot{M} \approx (1.2\text{--}1.9) \times 10^{-10}\,M_\odot\,\mathrm{yr^{-1}}$ via $L_{\rm X} \approx G M_{\rm wd}\dot{M}/R_{\rm wd}$.
papers.problem: The work investigates the energy budget and radiation mechanism of the highest-field polar AR UMa in high state, addressing why standard steady shock models predicting $L_{\rm reprocessed}/L_{\rm shock} \approx 0.5$ fail and lead to an apparent infinite soft X-ray excess without detected optically thin hard X-ray shock cooling emission.
papers.method: Multi-wavelength timing and phase-resolved spectral analysis utilizing XMM-Newton EPIC pn/MOS, RGS, and OM along with ground-based optical photometry. Spectral decomposition employs $\mathrm{Tbabs} \times (\mathrm{bbody} + 3\,\mathrm{apec})$ and blobby accretion dynamics governed by ram-to-magnetic pressure balance $\rho_s v_{\rm ff}(r)^2 \approx B(r)^2 / (8\pi)$ and photoelectric absorption $\tau_{\rm X} \propto \sigma(E) N_{\rm H}$ with $\sigma(E) \propto E^{-3}$.
papers.reason: This work presents comprehensive XMM-Newton X-ray/UV and optical observations of AR UMa ($B \approx 230\,\mathrm{MG}$), providing critical observational constraints on extreme magnetic accretion, diamagnetic blob fragmentation, and soft X-ray excess in compact object systems.

papers.title: Forecasting Fundamental-Plane Tests of Intermediate-mass Black Holes in Radio-selected Dwarf Galaxies
papers.result: For a $10^{6}\,M_{\odot}$ black hole point source at a $5\sigma$ threshold, current VLBA detection probabilities are $4.9\times 10^{-5}\text{--}0.029$ (ID 26), $0.03\text{--}0.06$ (ID 82), and $0.08\text{--}0.17$ (ID 83). Reaching $50\%$ completeness requires rms sensitivity $\sigma_{50}$ of $0.10\text{--}0.76\,\mu\mathrm{Jy\,beam^{-1}}$ (ID 26), $0.77\text{--}1.67\,\mu\mathrm{Jy\,beam^{-1}}$ (ID 82), and $3.37\text{--}8.31\,\mu\mathrm{Jy\,beam^{-1}}$ (ID 83). Extended structure attenuation scales as $\eta_{\theta}^{-1} = 1 + (\theta_s / \theta_b)^2$, which attenuates peak flux by factors of $\sim 13$, $33$, and $29$ for a $5\,\mathrm{pc}$ source.
papers.problem: Radio non-detections cannot be directly inverted into physical black hole mass upper limits because spatial filtering across intermediate physical scales ($\sim 1\text{--}100\,\mathrm{pc}$) between VLA and VLBA baselines, beam dilution, non-simultaneous variability, and astrometric offsets conflate non-detections with resolved-out flux or false host associations.
papers.method: A forward probabilistic framework is formulated using the Fundamental Plane relation $\ell_{R} = \xi_{RX}\ell_{X} + \mu_{\rm FP}m + b_{0}$ with Merloni calibration $(\xi_{RX},\mu_{\rm FP},b_0)=(0.60,0.78,7.33)$, where $\ell_R \equiv \log[\nu L_\nu(5\,\mathrm{GHz})/\mathrm{erg\,s^{-1}}]$, $\ell_X \equiv \log[L_{2-10\,\mathrm{keV}}/\mathrm{erg\,s^{-1}}]$, and $m \equiv \log(M_\bullet/M_\odot)$. The non-detection probability is computed via $P_{\rm nd}(m) = \int d\alpha\, d\ell_X\, d\ell_R\; p(\alpha)p(\ell_X)\mathcal{N}(\ell_R;\bar{\ell}_R,\sigma_R)\Phi\left[\frac{n_\sigma\sigma - \eta_\theta S_9(\ell_R,\alpha)}{\sigma}\right]$, incorporating beam dilution $\eta_\theta = \theta_b^2/(\theta_b^2+\theta_s^2)$, intrinsic scatter $\sigma_R$, and spectral index marginalization.
papers.reason: This work is relevant to compact object high-energy astrophysics and jet-accretion scaling relations, developing a rigorous forward-modeling framework to test intermediate-mass black holes in dwarf galaxies using the radio/X-ray Fundamental Plane.

papers.title: Superorbital period evolution of Hercules X-1
papers.result: The analysis finds that the superorbital period of Her X-1 is $P_{\rm sup} = 35.1(1)\text{ d}$ and exhibits a long-term secular decay rate of $\dot{P}_{\rm sup} = -4.7(1)\times 10^{-5}\text{ s s}^{-1}$ (with epoch folding yielding $\dot{P}_{\rm sup} = -5(2)\times 10^{-5}\text{ s s}^{-1}$), corresponding to a decay timescale of $P_{\rm sup}/|\dot{P}_{\rm sup}| \sim 1918\text{ yr}$; superimposed wanders on timescales of $10\text{--}38$ cycles show up to $\sim 5\%$ variation and correlate with X-ray count rate (Pearson $r = 0.73$).
papers.problem: Investigating whether the $\sim 35\text{ d}$ superorbital modulation in Hercules X-1 represents white-noise wandering around a fixed mean or a secular decay, and probing the physical mechanism between radiation-driven warped disc precession and neutron star free precession.
papers.method: Constructed a 30-to-50-year continuous light curve combining CGRO/BATSE, RXTE/ASM, Swift/BAT, Fermi/GBM, and MAXI/GSC; performed an epoch folding search in $P_{\rm sup}\text{--}\dot{P}_{\rm sup}$ parameter space, and modeled main-on peak arrivals with quadratic $O-C$ fitting using $O_n = C_0 + n P_{\rm sup} + \frac{n^2}{2!} P_{\rm sup} \dot{P}_{\rm sup}$.
papers.reason: This paper presents multi-decadal X-ray timing observations of the accreting pulsar Hercules X-1, offering valuable observational constraints on compact object superorbital period evolution and neutron star precession.

papers.method: BaseCat2 contains 2086 bursts and 1748 independent sources, stacked on foreground halos using $\mathrm{DM}=\int_0^z n_e(z')(1+z')^{-1}dl$ and $\Delta\mathrm{DM}_{\mathrm{egal}}=\mathrm{DM}-\mathrm{DM}_{\mathrm{MW}}$. The radial analysis uses $b_{\min}/r_{\rm CGM}$, Gaussian bin-membership weights, and the fit $n_e^{\rm CGM}(r)=n_{e,0}[1+(r/r_c)^2]^{-3\beta/2}$. SLOW and Simba comparisons test alternative contributions, while $\eta_{\mathrm{CGM}}=\mathrm{DM}_{\mathrm{CGM}}/\mathrm{DM}_{\mathrm{cosmic}}$ forecasts favorable redshifts.
papers.reason: This directly constrains the circumgalactic contribution to FRB dispersion measure using the second CHIME/FRB baseband catalog, including a radial and mass-dependent DM stack relevant to FRB sightline environments.

papers.title: Scalable early warning for binary neutron-star mergers in third-generation gravitational-wave detectors
papers.result: A CNN with $\mathcal{N}=10^{3}$ templates reaches a sensitivity distance comparable to SFT matched filtering, which instead needs approximately $\mathcal{N}_{\mathrm{SFT}}=10^{7}$ templates, about four orders of magnitude more. For $f_{\max}=10\,\mathrm{Hz}$ and $f_{\min}\in\{2,3,4,5\}\,\mathrm{Hz}$, the quoted evaluation time falls from minutes to milliseconds, a speed-up of about $1.6\times10^{4}$–$4.0\times10^{4}$; the CNN per-template cost is $\langle\mathfrak{c}_1\rangle\approx(3$–$25)\,\mu\mathrm{s}$. At fixed template number, sensitivity follows $\langle s\rangle\sim\rho_{\rm opt}^{2}(1-\langle\mu\rangle)$ with $\rho_{\rm opt}^{2}\propto\int_{f_{\min}}^{10\,\mathrm{Hz}}f^{-7/3}/S_n(f)\,df$.
papers.problem: Early warning of binary neutron-star inspirals in third-generation detectors is limited by the computing cost of evaluating the detection statistic at low latency.
papers.method: Early inspirals are represented by narrowband SFTs with $T_{\mathrm{SFT}}=31\,\mathrm{s}$ and $\Delta k=51$ bins about $f(t;\mathcal{M}_{\mathrm{c}})=f_{\max}[1+(256/5)(\pi f_{\max})^{8/3}(G\mathcal{M}_{\mathrm{c}}/c^{3})^{5/3}(t_{\max}-t)]^{-3/8}$. A CNN minimizes binary cross-entropy and searches only $\mathcal{M}_{\mathrm{c}}$, while the SFT statistic $\mathcal{X}$ is maximized analytically over phase and luminosity distance and then over an eight-dimensional bank. Latency is modeled as $\mathcal{C}=\mathcal{N}\langle\mathfrak{c}_1\rangle$, with $f_s=40\,\mathrm{Hz}$ for the 3, 4, and 5 Hz regimes.
papers.reason: This is a low-latency BNS early-warning search method for third-generation detectors, useful for compact-object multi-messenger follow-up, but it does not directly study FRB/PRS, supernova engines, jets, neutrinos, or circumstellar interaction.

papers.title: A panchromatic photometric and spectroscopic modeling of SN1987A from 200 to 800d
papers.result: For $Z_\odot/3$ models with $M_{\rm init}=11$–$21\,M_\odot$, fixed $E_{\rm kin}=1.2\times10^{51}\,\mathrm{erg}$, and $M(^{56}\mathrm{Ni})=0.07$–$0.08\,M_\odot$, late-time metallicity effects are weak. $[{\rm O\,I}]\,\lambda\lambda 6300.3,6363.8$ rises from 11 to $17\,M_\odot$ and then falls for $M_{\rm init}\gtrsim17$–$19\,M_\odot$; th11 and th21 have similar line fluxes despite O yields of $0.32$ versus $2.58\,M_\odot$. Assigning 90% of C/O-shell cooling to CO lowers the line by $\sim10$–$20\%$ and can underestimate $M_{\rm init}$ by $\sim1\,M_\odot$. Without strong CO/SiO cooling, $13\,M_\odot$ (O yield $0.79\,M_\odot$) fits best. $\gamma$-rays are fully trapped at 200 d, but by 800 d only $\sim20\%$ (th11) to $\sim50\%$ (th21) of the decay power is absorbed; th13 has $\tau_{\rm es}=1.28\rightarrow0.011$ and $L\sim10^{41}\rightarrow10^{38}\,\mathrm{erg\,s^{-1}}$. Dust, not smooth $\gamma$-ray leakage, explains the post-500 d excess fading of $\sim1.5\,\mathrm{mag}$: $0.1\,\mu\mathrm{m}$ silicates with $M_{\rm d}=10^{-4}$, $4\times10^{-3}$, and $5\times10^{-3}\,M_\odot$ at 600, 700, and 800 d, placed at $v<2000\,\mathrm{km\,s^{-1}}$, keep the $V$ offset within $0.2\,\mathrm{mag}$ and are optically thick from the UV through the IR.
papers.problem: The work asks which progenitor mass is allowed by the nebular spectra of SN 1987A and whether the post-500 d optical deficit and UV behavior come from $\gamma$-ray leakage, molecular cooling, newly formed internal dust, or background-star contamination, rather than from circumstellar interaction.
papers.method: One-dimensional, time-dependent NLTE radiative transfer with CMFGEN uses shuffled-shell macroscopic mixing and no microscopic mixing. The only power source is radioactive decay, dominated by the $^{56}\mathrm{Ni}$ chain, with nonlocal $\gamma$-ray deposition at gray opacity $\kappa_\gamma=0.06\,Y_e\,\mathrm{cm^{2}\,g^{-1}}$. Molecules are omitted in the global solution; a CO test retains only 10% of the C/O-shell absorbed decay power. After $\sim500\,\mathrm{d}$, $0.1\,\mu\mathrm{m}$ silicate dust is added only inside the metal-rich region at $v<2000\,\mathrm{km\,s^{-1}}$. Spectra are placed at $D=49.59\,\mathrm{kpc}$ with $E(B-V)=0.15\,\mathrm{mag}$, and model comparisons are normalized by absorbed decay power.
papers.reason: The paper quantifies radioactive-decay-powered nebular emission, progenitor-mass diagnostics, and internal dust in SN 1987A at 200–800 d, which is useful for separating engine yields and dust from circumstellar interaction, but it does not model the interaction, jets, or neutrinos.

papers.title: Current Closure and Gamma-Ray Signatures of Spark-Gap and Current-Sheet Activities in Radiative Black Hole Magnetospheres
papers.result: A polar spark gap and a variable equatorial current sheet jointly sustain the global poloidal current. With low pair multiplicity, synchrotron–curvature (SC) cooling leaves the overall structure largely unchanged but drives spark-gap electric-field oscillations; polar and equatorial variability have no significant cross-correlation and $\Delta t\sim l_{\rm rec}/(\mathcal{R}_{\rm in}c)\sim 10\,r_{\rm g}/c$ at $\mathcal{R}_{\rm in}\sim +0.1$. Post-processed bolometric luminosities are $L_{\rm IC}\sim 10^{-4}L_{\rm BZ}$ and $L_{\rm SC}\sim 10^{-2}L_{\rm BZ}$ (reported in the opening summary as SC up to $\sim 1\%$ and inverse Compton $\sim 0.1\%$ of the BZ luminosity), with spark-gap photons reaching sub-TeV energies. Balancing $t_{\rm SC}=6\pi m_{\rm e}c/(\sigma_{\rm T}f_{\perp,\rm eff}^{2}B_{0}^{2}\Gamma)$ and $t_{\rm acc}\approx\Gamma m_{\rm e}c/(ef_{D}B_{0})$ gives $\Gamma_{\rm max}=\sqrt{f_{D}/f_{\perp,\rm eff}^{2}}\,\Gamma_{\rm SC}\simeq 3.7\times 10^{6}$ for representative equatorial $B_{0}\sim 10^{2}\,\mathrm{G}$.
papers.problem: The paper investigates how a polar spark gap and an equatorial current sheet jointly close the global poloidal current in a radiative, charge-starved Kerr black-hole magnetosphere, and how SC cooling changes particle acceleration, variability, and gamma-ray signatures relative to observed VHE flares.
papers.method: The study uses axisymmetric 2D GRPIC in Kerr–Schild 3+1 form, evolving $\frac{1}{c}\partial_t\bm{B}=-\nabla\times\bm{E}$ and $\frac{1}{c}\partial_t\bm{D}=\nabla\times\bm{H}-\frac{4\pi}{c}\bm{J}$ with Hamiltonian particles, ambient-photon inverse Compton scattering, and two-photon pair creation. It compares no cooling, $\Gamma_{\rm SC}=\infty$, with marginal slow cooling, $\Gamma_{\rm SC}=800$, from a Wald vertical field at $a=0.99$, $\tilde{B}_{0}=5\times 10^{3}$, $\varepsilon_{0}=5\times 10^{-2}$, and $\tau_{0}=10$ ($\sigma_{0}\simeq 1.2\times 10^{4}$), followed by ray tracing. The SC drag is $\bm{g}\simeq-\frac{2}{3}\frac{e^{4}}{m_{\rm e}^{2}c^{4}}\Gamma^{2}\bm{\beta}B_{\perp,\rm eff}^{2}$.
papers.reason: This radiative Kerr-magnetosphere GRPIC study is useful for relativistic-jet launching and compact-object VHE emission because it quantifies current closure and gamma-ray output relative to the Blandford–Znajek power, but it is peripheral to FRB, pulsar-wind, and supernova-engine problems.

papers.title: SMMAN studies of AGN variability. II. Radio and optical quasi-periodic oscillations and changing variability states in the relativistic jet of the blazar PKS 0754+100
papers.result: Radio QPOs detected at $278\pm3$ days (4.8 GHz, global $2.98\sigma$) and $292\pm6$ days (23.6 GHz, global $3.5\sigma$); optical QPO at $1.4\pm0.1$ days (TESS, global $2.87\sigma$); state transition near MJD 59500 with RMS increase from 0.1 to 0.28 Jy at 23.6 GHz.
papers.problem: Origin of long-term radio and short-term optical QPOs together with changing variability states in the relativistic jet of BL Lac PKS 0754+100 at $z=0.266$.
papers.method: Detrended light curves analyzed with GLSP and WWZ; significance via 100000 STINGRAY simulations of broken power-law PSD $P(f)$ under red-noise null hypothesis; trial factor $T=M\times S$ for global significance.
papers.reason: Reports multi-band QPO detections and variability state transition in blazar relativistic jet, providing incremental constraints on jet instabilities and precession models.

papers.title: Stochastic Acceleration Downstream of Astrophysical Shocks
papers.result: Stochastic acceleration appreciably changes the downstream particle spectrum whenever $\eta \gtrsim \xi_{\rm CR}$. For standard Model I parameters, including stochastic acceleration and wave feedback increases the gamma-ray flux between $\sim 1$ and $100\,\mathrm{GeV}$ by $\sim 50\%$. For an undamped $f(p)\propto p^{-4}$ Kolmogorov cascade, $P t_{\rm age}/P_{\rm CR}\approx (3/4)\eta/\xi_{\rm CR}$; acceleration times scale as $\tau_{\rm acc}\sim p^{1/3}$ (Kolmogorov) or $\sim p^{1/2}$ (Kraichnan), while source-free inertial spectra are $W\sim k^{-5/3}$ and $W\sim k^{-3/2}$. Upstream self-generated waves alone do not significantly modify the downstream spectrum because the cascade rapidly removes their energy.
papers.problem: The paper asks whether particles accelerated at an SNR shock and then advected downstream have their spectrum modified by second-order Fermi acceleration, and whether that change appears in $pp\to\pi^0$ gamma rays, despite strong-shock DSA spectra being nearly universal for $M_s\gg 1$.
papers.method: The particle distribution and turbulent spectrum are evolved together through $\partial_t f=p^{-2}\partial_p(p^2 D_{pp}\partial_p f)$ and $\partial_t W+\partial_k F=-\Gamma W+S-D$, using quasi-linear $D_{pp}$, resonant damping $\Gamma$, and Kolmogorov or Kraichnan cascades. The SNR downstream is split into independent shells with adiabatic losses, and the $pp$ gamma-ray flux is integrated with Naima and Kafexhiu cross sections, comparing cases with and without stochastic acceleration and wave feedback.
papers.reason: The paper quantifies when downstream second-order Fermi acceleration at SNR shocks can reshape cosmic-ray spectra and the associated pp gamma-ray flux, which is useful for supernova-shock and high-energy studies, but it does not treat central engines, shock breakout, FRBs, or jets.

papers.title: The Fate of Collisional Neutrino Flavor Conversion: Fixed Points, Period Doubling, and Chaos
papers.result: Homogeneous collective precession (HCP) is a rotating-frame fixed point, but it is not always attracting. As the electron collision rate $\kappa_e$ approaches $0.0025$ from below, the target growth rate and the HCP number offset vanish together (supercritical Hopf); near $\kappa_e\simeq0.018$ a finite-amplitude pair appears, and the unstable branch merges with the target near $\kappa_e\simeq0.0221$ (subcritical Hopf). An independent HCP crossing occurs at $\kappa_e\simeq0.0200194578$, before target destabilization at $\kappa_e\simeq0.0221481171$. For $0.034\le\kappa_e\le0.060$, successive maxima of $P_z$ period-double eight times toward a stable $256$-cycle, with spacing ratios approaching $\delta_{\rm F}\simeq4.669$. At $\kappa_e=0.055025$ the leading Lyapunov estimate is $\widehat\lambda_1\simeq2.8\times10^{-3}$ for bounded irregular evolution. The HCP balance is $s(u^\star)^2=z^\star\tau^\star$, while averages obey $s[\langle u\rangle_T^2+\mathrm{Var}_T(u)]=\langle z\rangle_T\langle Z\rangle_T+\mathrm{Cov}_T(z,Z)-\tfrac12\mathcal{B}_{u^2}$. The largest reported HCP-versus-time-average population deviation is $8.03\%$, set by the mean coherent torque rather than by stationarity.
papers.problem: The issue is whether a collisionally balanced HCP state attracts neutrino flavor trajectories or whether collisional flavor instability instead produces Hopf cycles, period doubling, and chaos, and how far HCP or mean-only estimates miss the time-averaged flavor populations.
papers.method: The full quantum kinetic equations are linearized in the rotating frame, including the response of the self-interaction field; after removal of the common phase, local attraction requires all seven Jacobian eigenvalues to have negative real parts. For energy-independent rates the collective matrix follows the monochromatic kinetics and residuals contract at least as $e^{-\kappa_* t}$. Root number is fixed by the sign of $\mathcal{C}$, and $\kappa_e$ is scanned with multiple shooting and Lyapunov estimates. Steady balance is $s(u^\star)^2=z^\star\tau^\star$, whereas the time-averaged identity keeps $\mathrm{Var}_T(u)$ and $\mathrm{Cov}_T(z,Z)$.
papers.reason: The paper is relevant to supernova and compact-merger neutrino transport because collisional flavor conversion need not settle to an attracting fixed point, and the resulting cycles or chaos shift time-averaged flavor populations. It is worth knowing rather than essential because it is a specialized kinetic bifurcation study, not a direct engine or high-energy observational constraint.

papers.title: Unveiling a Concentration of Hard X-Ray Point Sources in the Nuclear Stellar Disk with XMM-Newton
papers.result: Within the NSD ($|l|\lesssim 1.3^{\circ}$, $|b|\lesssim 0.3^{\circ}$), XMM-Newton finds a concentration of intrinsically hard point sources. Plane sources are softer, with mean $\mathrm{HR}\simeq 0.1$ (PN) and $\simeq-0.3$ (MOS), where $\mathrm{HR}\equiv(H-S)/(H+S)$, $H=4.5$–$12\,\mathrm{keV}$, and $S=2.0$–$4.5\,\mathrm{keV}$. Inside-versus-outside HR distributions differ at $>8\sigma$. At $-1.05^{\circ}<l<0.55^{\circ}$, observed $\mathrm{HR}\gtrsim 0.3$ exceeds $\mathrm{HR}<0.2$ predicted for $5\times10^{22}<N_{\rm H}<8\times10^{22}\,\mathrm{cm}^{-2}$. Hard and soft longitude/latitude distributions differ at $>12\sigma/9\sigma$ ($p=2\times10^{-35}/3\times10^{-20}$). Scale heights are $h_{l,\rm s}=2^{\circ}$ ($\sim280\,\mathrm{pc}$), $h_{b,\rm s}=0.31^{\circ}$ ($\sim44\,\mathrm{pc}$), $h_{l,\rm h}=0.66^{\circ}$ ($\sim90\,\mathrm{pc}$), and $h_{b,\rm h}=0.17^{\circ}$ ($\sim24\,\mathrm{pc}$). The stellar-mass distribution follows the soft sources better than the hard sources. The hard NSD population most likely consists of intermediate polars with high $M_{\rm WD}$, possibly plus MSPs; representative partial covering at $kT=36\,\mathrm{keV}$ gives $\mathrm{HR}\sim0.82$ versus $\sim0.36$ without it, and $\langle kT\rangle\approx34\,\mathrm{keV}$ for IPs versus $\approx11\,\mathrm{keV}$ for polars. The $\log N$–$\log S$ slope is $\alpha\sim1.35$–$1.5$.
papers.problem: The paper tests whether the hard X-ray point-source concentration overlapping the NSD is an intrinsically harder compact-object population or only an artifact of large line-of-sight $N_{\rm H}$, and what that population implies for the unresolved sources underlying the Galactic-center and Galactic-ridge X-ray emission.
papers.method: Using the XMM-Newton Heritage Survey and cleaned 4XMM-DR14 sources over $|l|<10^{\circ}$, $|b|<1^{\circ}$, the authors compare $\mathrm{HR}\equiv(H-S)/(H+S)$ inside and outside the NSD with count-rate and exposure-matched K–S tests. Because most sources lack reliable spectra, they simulate 274 parameter sets with XSPEC fakeit and EPIC-PN responses: $\mathrm{tbabs}\times\mathrm{powerlaw}$ for $\Gamma=0$–$3$ and absorbed APEC for $kT=1$–$36\,\mathrm{keV}$, spanning $N_{\rm H}=(1$–$30)\times10^{22}\,\mathrm{cm}^{-2}$ and $Z_{\rm Fe}=(0.5,1,2)Z_{\odot}$.
papers.reason: The paper establishes an intrinsic hard X-ray point-source excess in the Nuclear Stellar Disk and associates it with high-mass white-dwarf intermediate polars and possibly millisecond pulsars, which is relevant compact-object high-energy context but not central to FRB, jet, neutrino, or supernova-engine studies.

papers.title: The shape and velocity of black hole coronas
papers.result: IXPE measures a 2–8 keV polarization of $(4.01\pm 0.20)\%$ parallel to the radio jet at inclination $27.51^\circ$, whereas static corona models give only $1$–$2.5\%$. Cylindrical outflow models with $h=H/(2R)\leq 0.8$ and $\beta_{\rm top}=0.5$–$0.9$ simultaneously give $\Gamma=1.6$ and $\sim 4\%$ polarization parallel to the symmetry axis; larger $h$ has $q_{\rm max}<4\%$ even at $\beta_{\rm top}=0.99$. Outflow suppresses radiative feedback as $f_\beta\propto(1-\beta)^2$. The discussion gives $\delta\approx 1.56$, $L\approx 0.3L_{\rm iso}$, $\ell=35.4(L_{\rm iso}/0.5\%L_{\rm Edd})(r_g/R)$, $t_{\rm IC}=0.03(R/r_g)R/c$, $B_{\rm eq}\approx 1.1\times 10^{7}(R/r_g)^{-1}\,\mathrm{G}$, $\sigma\approx 6.9(R/r_g)^{-1}$ and $v_A\approx 0.9c$, favoring a pair corona. The IXPE polarization-angle difference is $3.3^\circ\pm 3.2^\circ$; requiring the band-to-band Faraday difference to be $<0.11$ rad yields $\eta_\Delta<0.14(B_\parallel/10^{7}\,\mathrm{G})^{-1}$.
papers.problem: Static Comptonizing coronae underpredict the hard-state polarization of Cyg X-1: IXPE finds about $4\%$ polarization parallel to the radio jet, while static models give only $1$–$2.5\%$. The question is how small $h=H/(2R)$ must be and how fast an axial outflow must be to reproduce both $\Gamma=1.6$ and the polarization.
papers.method: polrad-3D Monte Carlo polarized transfer is run in a three-dimensional cylinder with the symmetry axis along $z$, temporarily neglecting general relativity. Continuity gives $n(z)\propto\beta^{-1}$, with Thomson depths $t_z=\bar{n}\sigma_T H$ and $t_r=\bar{n}\sigma_T R$. Constant-$\beta$ and accelerating profiles from $\beta_0=0.1$ to $\beta_{\rm top}$ are compared for a $100\,\mathrm{keV}$ Maxwell–Jüttner plasma and unpolarized isotropic $10\,\mathrm{eV}$ cyclo-synchrotron seeds, using invariant optical depth and the full Klein–Nishina Fano matrix. Grids in $t_z$ and $\beta_{\rm top}$, with up to $6.4\times 10^8$ photons, are matched to $\Gamma=1.6$ and $q=4\%$ at $i=27.5^\circ$.
papers.reason: IXPE polarization and spectral constraints on the Cyg X-1 corona’s aspect ratio and axial outflow are relevant to compact-object high-energy observations and jet-aligned geometry, but the work is peripheral to FRB, supernova-engine, and shock-breakout studies.

papers.problem: Earlier full-plane IceCube searches reached about $4.5\sigma$ and $5.7\sigma$ using GeV--TeV gamma-ray templates. The question is how the neutrino normalization and spectral index vary with Galactic longitude without assuming an emission model, and whether that spectrum matches hadronic gamma-ray data.

papers.title: Reabsorbed Urca neutrinos suppress bulk-viscous damping of neutron star merger oscillations
papers.result: An energy-resolved kinetic treatment gives a damping time of 2.7 s for a 1 kHz, 10 km oscillation at nuclear density and 4 MeV, against 19 ms for freely escaping neutrinos. For remnant kHz modes the composition is nearly frozen, so the Urca channel damps them on seconds rather than tens of milliseconds; sampled DD2 states give mean capture energies 19–46 MeV and emission-weighted absorption lengths below 7 m. The kinetic time cannot fall below the transparent resonance minimum $\tau_{\rm res}=2K_{T}B/(C^{2}\omega)$.
papers.problem: Transparent Urca bulk viscosity was expected to damp neutron-star-merger density oscillations within tens of milliseconds when the relaxation rate matches the mode frequency, but that estimate treats only thermal-energy neutrinos as free-streaming and omits reabsorption of much harder sub-threshold capture neutrinos.
papers.method: DD2 $npe\mu$ matter is evolved at fixed cold $\beta$-equilibrium composition with direct Urca from momentum-resolved phase space, modified Urca in the Fermi-surface approximation, and isotropic elastic neutral-current scattering. Linear energy-resolved kinetics define an admittance $\Lambda(\omega,k)$, effective bulk viscosity $\zeta_{\rm eff}(\omega,k)=C^{2}{\rm Re}\Lambda/|-i\omega+B\Lambda|^{2}$, and damping time $\tau=K_T/(\zeta_{\rm eff}\omega^{2})$, using $C=n(\partial\Delta\mu/\partial n)_{T,Y_e,Y_\mu}$, $B=-(\partial\Delta\mu/\partial n_e)_{n,T,Y_\mu}$, and $K_T=n(\partial p/\partial n)_{T,Y_e,Y_\mu}$.
papers.reason: Reabsorption of sub-threshold Urca neutrinos removes the resonant bulk-viscous damping of kHz neutron-star-merger oscillations, a quantitative neutrino-transport result for compact remnants that is adjacent to, but not a direct test of, FRB, supernova-engine, or jet models.

papers.title: GRB 241030A: A fallback-accreting magnetar description of the early X-ray emission
papers.result: For GRB 241030A at $z=1.411$, the descriptive fallback-magnetar candidate has $P_0\simeq4.25\,\mathrm{ms}$, $B\simeq3.04\times10^{15}\,\mathrm{G}$, source-frame $t_{\rm fb}\simeq143\,\mathrm{s}$, $M_{\rm norm}=0.0090M_\odot$ and $\epsilon_{\rm eff}=81.2$. At observer time 200 s it is an ejector, with $P_*=4.816\,\mathrm{ms}$, $r_{\rm m}=234.8\,\mathrm{km}>r_{\rm LC}=229.8\,\mathrm{km}$, $N_{\rm acc}=0$, $L_{\rm EM}=2.973\times10^{48}\,\mathrm{erg\,s^{-1}}$ and $F_{\rm mag}=1.902\times10^{-8}\,\mathrm{erg\,cm^{-2}\,s^{-1}}$. The correlated-residual medians are $P_0=16.8\,\mathrm{ms}$ (68 per cent interval 2.76–286 ms), $B=1.56\times10^{15}\,\mathrm{G}$, $t_{\rm fb}=54.8\,\mathrm{s}$ and $\epsilon_{\rm eff}=2.34$. Only 79 of 380 fluxes lie in the central 90 per cent predictive intervals, while 301 lie above them.
papers.problem: The paper asks whether the bright, variable unabsorbed 0.3–10 keV emission of GRB 241030A at observer times about 80–430 s, before the smoother afterglow, contains a sustained fallback-accreting magnetar contribution.
papers.method: The star is evolved with $I_\ast d\Omega_\ast/dt=N_{\rm acc}-N_{\rm EM}$ and $\dot{M}_{\rm fb}(t)=\dot{M}_0[(t/t_{\rm fb})^{-1/2}+(t/t_{\rm fb})^{5/3}]^{-1}$, using $r_m=\xi[9\mu^4/(4GM_\ast\dot{M}_{\rm fb}^2)]^{1/7}$, $\omega_s=(r_m/r_{\rm co})^{3/2}$ and $L_{\rm EM}=\kappa_\chi\mu^2\Omega_\ast^2/(c r_Y^2)$. The observed flux is $F_{\rm mag}=\epsilon_{\rm eff}L_{\rm EM}/(4\pi D_L^2)$ with $D_L=10.30\,\mathrm{Gpc}$, fit directly to 380 unabsorbed 0.3–10 keV XRT bins from 80 to 430 s.
papers.reason: The paper is relevant to long-GRB central engines because it tests a fallback-accreting magnetar against the bright early X-ray emission of GRB 241030A. Its own posterior checks underpredict the flux and variability and leave the birth spin unconstrained, so the result is conditional rather than a definitive engine identification.

papers.title: NS 1987A: A Potential Probe of Crustal Superfluidity with Future X-ray Observations
papers.result:
Without fast neutrino cooling such as direct Urca, the adopted Lynx-like window (about $0.5''$ and effective area $\sim 2\,\mathrm{m}^{2}$ at $1\,\mathrm{keV}$) yields detection at $t\sim 60\,\mathrm{yr}$ (about 2047). Weak inner-crust neutron superfluidity leaves a non-isothermal profile at detection. Direct Urca generally disfavors detection, except near-threshold “meteor” models such as $1.36\,M_\odot$. Defining $t_{\mathrm{relax}}$ as the age in $1<t<200\,\mathrm{yr}$ that maximizes $\left|d\ln L_\gamma^\infty/d\ln tight|$, $t_{\mathrm{obs}}<t_{\mathrm{relax}}$ means the inner crust is hotter than the core. For CCDK, $t_{\mathrm{obs}}\sim 60\,\mathrm{yr}$ except Y+K models with $M\gtrsim 1.40\,M_\odot$, where $t_{\mathrm{obs}}\approx 202\,\mathrm{yr}$. For $T_{c,n3}\lesssim 7	imes 10^{8}\,\mathrm{K}$, $L_\gamma$ is nearly unchanged over $200\,\mathrm{yr}$. A polar dipole $\sim 3	imes 10^{15}\,\mathrm{G}$ can raise $L_\gamma^\infty\sim 5	imes 10^{35}\,\mathrm{erg\,s^{-1}}$ by Joule heating. Proton superconductivity shortens the direct-Urca cooling time by $\sim 50\,\mathrm{yr}$ and shifts the minimal-cooling detection age by $\sim 10\,\mathrm{yr}$, chiefly because $\kappa_e=\pi^{2}k_B^{2}Tn_e/(3m_e^{*}
u_e)$ increases, with $
u_e\simeq
u_{ee}+
u_{ep}$.
papers.problem: The paper investigates whether the thermal X-ray detection age of NS 1987A precedes crust-core isothermality, allowing inner-crust neutron superfluidity to be probed, and how direct Urca and proton superconductivity move that age relative to the sensitivity window.
papers.method: Cooling sequences vary the EOS (APR and Y+K), $M_{\mathrm{NS}}\simeq 1.2$–$1.6\,M_\odot$, inner-crust $^1S_0$ models, and envelope parameter $\eta\equiv g_{14}M_{\mathrm{env}}/M_{\mathrm{NS}}=10^{-8},10^{-7}$. papers.title: Early--Narrow and Late--Wide Populations of GRB X-ray Flares
papers.result: A rest-frame GMM of $(t_{\rm pk},w)$ yields two populations: early–narrow (~80%, $\langle t_{\rm pk}\rangle\simeq10^{2}\,{\rm s}$, $w/t_{\rm pk}\lesssim1$; center $\log_{10}(t_{\rm pk},w)=(1.97,1.85)$) and late–wide (~20%, $\langle t_{\rm pk}\rangle\simeq10^{3.5}\,{\rm s}$, $w/t_{\rm pk}\gtrsim2$; center $(3.49,3.80)$). Their mean energies are consistent, $\langle\log_{10}(E_{\rm iso,f,rest})\rangle=51.13\pm0.10$ versus $50.66\pm0.20$ (K–S $p=0.22$). Early–narrow flares follow $L_{\rm avg,f,rest}\propto t_{\rm pk,rest}^{-1.74^{+0.24}_{-0.24}}$, while late–wide flares give $-0.19^{+1.01}_{-0.93}$; the combined slope is $-1.60^{+0.12}_{-0.12}$, shallower than $L_{\rm pk}\propto t_{\rm pk}^{-3}$. The global fit $\log w_{\rm rest}=\alpha+\beta\log t_{\rm pk,rest}$ has $\beta=1.21^{+0.06}_{-0.06}$, but only early–narrow flares are significant ($\beta=1.04^{+0.12}_{-0.13}$, $w/t_{\rm pk}\sim0.76$ versus $\sim2.04$). Waiting times are $\sim76\,{\rm s}$ versus $\sim2950\,{\rm s}$.

papers.method: Light curves from 100 redshift-known Swift-BAT GRBs (89 fitted; 61 with flares) are modeled with asymmetric Norris profiles. A multivariate GMM classifies $(t_{\rm pk},w)$; K–S, Spearman, and Bayesian regression test relations. Luminosity is $L_{\rm avg,f,rest}=E_{\rm iso,f,rest}/w_{\rm rest}$, and accretion timing is compared with $t_{\rm visc}\sim\alpha^{-1}(H/R)^{-2}\Omega_K^{-1}$.

papers.title: New Constraints on the Ultrahigh Energy Neutrino Flux from the First Array-Wide Search with the Askaryan Radio Array
papers.result: The array-wide diffuse search observes $n=0$ events against an expected background of $0.13\pm 0.01$ (stat.) $^{+0.05}_{-0.06}$ (syst.). The Feldman–Cousins $90\%$ CL limit is the strongest among techniques over $50$–$1000\,\mathrm{EeV}$. Analysis-level expectations are $\mu=5.3$ (Global UL; $2.6\sigma$, $99\%$ exclusion), $\mu=2.4$ (Muzio; $1.3\sigma$, $90\%$ exclusion), $\mu=1.6$ (KM3NeT; $0.8\sigma$, $77\%$), $\mu=0.4$ (Kotera; $27\%$), and $\mu=0.2$ for both $100\%$ protons and Fang pulsars ($<1\%$). papers.method: ARA stations A1–A5 plus the A5 phased array are analyzed from January 2013 through December 2023, corresponding to $28$ station-years ($25.9$ after quality cuts; $10.6$ array-equivalent years). Each string uses $150$–$850\,\mathrm{MHz}$ antennas with station triggers kept at $\le 5$ events/s and the phased array at $\le 11$ events/s. Sensitivity for $50$ configurations is computed with NuLeptonSim and AraSim for an $E^{-1}$ spectrum. Cuts were set on a random $10\%$ sample with the remaining $90\%$ blinded; surface and thermal cuts retain $56\%$ and $85\%$ of simulated $E^{-1}$ neutrinos, and the benchmark-flux efficiency is $28\%$. Models are tested with $p=\mathrm{Poiss}(n=0\mid\mu)$ and Feldman–Cousins $90\%$ CL limits.

papers.title: Spectral Constraints on Line-Seed Inverse-Compton Models for the MeV Feature in GRB 221009A
papers.result: No line-seed inverse-Compton candidate is shown to satisfy photon supply, relative components, LAT consistency, and escape together. In the observer-directed Thomson limit, $\epsilon^{\rm IC}_{\rm obs}\simeq 2\gamma_e^2\epsilon(1-\beta_e\mu_i)/(1+z)$, while a head-on collision approaches $4\gamma_e^2\epsilon/(1+z)$. For host-frame $Ly\alpha\simeq 10.2\,{\rm eV}$ and $H\alpha\simeq 1.89\,{\rm eV}$, scattering to $10\,{\rm MeV}$ needs $\gamma_{e,Ly\alpha}\simeq 531$ and $\gamma_{e,H\alpha}\simeq 1.23\times 10^3$. A log-normal electron distribution seeded by H$_2$ $2.122\,\mu{\rm m}$ ($0.584\,{\rm eV}$) matches two published intervals at $E_{\rm c,H_2}=11.5$ and $8.8\,{\rm MeV}$, with $\gamma_0=3.30\times 10^3$ and $2.69\times 10^3$ and $s_\gamma=0.087$ and $0.177$; the corresponding trial UV centroids are about $210$ and $161\,{\rm MeV}$ with standard deviations about $35$ and $55\,{\rm MeV}$. None of 40 molecular combinations lies below the adopted central envelope at all sampled energies, and trace minima are about $3.46$, $1.48$, $1.60$, and $1.40$. Even under ideal excitation and internal escape, compact reference-line densities fall short by factors of approximately $4$–$9$; precursor-assisted deficits remain at least about $4.3$, or about $87$–$1.7\times 10^2$ for single photon use. A decreasing centroid does not uniquely imply electron deceleration, and the four-interval calibration $\gamma_0\simeq(3.30,2.70,1.62,2.08)\times 10^3$ is non-monotonic.
papers.problem: Can H$_2$ ultraviolet-fluorescence photons, hydrogen recombination lines, or metal K-shell lines, scattered once by relativistic electrons, explain the Fermi-GBM MeV feature of GRB 221009A without violating the simultaneous LAT spectrum, local photon supply, timing, angular geometry, and the adopted spectral envelope?
papers.method: The model uses anisotropic single-scattering kinematics and a Klein–Nishina emissivity. With recoil parameter $b\equiv 4\gamma_e\epsilon/(m_ec^2)$, the local response is $d\ln\epsilon^{\rm IC}_{\rm obs}/d\ln\epsilon=1/(1+b)$. The flux is $F_{\epsilon_{\rm obs}}(\epsilon_{\rm obs},t_{\rm obs})=\frac{1+z}{d_L^2}\int d^3\boldsymbol{r}\,j_{\rm IC}[(1+z)\epsilon_{\rm obs},\Omega_{\rm s},\boldsymbol{r},t_{\rm ret}]e^{-\tau_{\rm esc}}$, integrated on equal-arrival-time surfaces with $dt_{\rm obs}=(1+z)(1-\beta_e\mu_{\rm s})dt$. Electrons follow $\frac{dN_e}{d\ln\gamma_e}=\frac{N_e}{\sqrt{2\pi}s_\gamma}\exp\left[-\frac{(\ln\gamma_e-\ln\gamma_0)^2}{2s_\gamma^2}\right]$; $\gamma_0$ and $s_\gamma$ are calibrated to photon moments, and 40 PDR-template plus external-screen combinations are compared with reconstructed central spectra. Optically thin component ratios scale as $\frac{F_{2,B_2}}{F_{1,B_1}}=\frac{u_2}{u_1}\frac{\mathcal{P}_{2,B_2}}{\mathcal{P}_{1,B_1}}$.
papers.reason: This paper quantitatively tests whether atomic and molecular line photons, inverse-Compton scattered in a relativistic outflow, can produce the evolving MeV feature of GRB 221009A, a direct constraint on jet radiation and dense circumstellar or molecular seed supply.

papers.title: Detectability of Seyfert galaxies in point-source and stacking searches with a global network of neutrino telescopes
papers.result: In all three scenarios the Circinus Galaxy is by far the brightest southern Seyfert in both neutrinos and MeV $\gamma$-rays. If Seyferts supply the diffuse astrophysical neutrino flux up to ${\sim}100\,\mathrm{TeV}$ and Circinus has at least the population-average neutrino luminosity, the IceCube--Baikal-GVD--KM3NeT/ARCA--P-ONE network reaches $5\sigma$ on Circinus by 2038 at the latest; Appendix C gives ${\sim}6.1\sigma$ (NGC 1068-like, $5\sigma$ in 2033) and ${\sim}6.2\sigma$ (average, $5\sigma$ in 2038) by 2040. The scenarios are $(P_{\mathrm{CR}}/P_{\mathrm{th}},\eta)=(0.5,56)$ (NGC 1068-like), $(0.01,1)$ (average), and $(0.5,1)$ (optimistic), with $\eta=B^{2}/\delta B^{2}$. Using NGC 1068 parameters for every source exceeds the TeV diffuse flux by $3.8\sigma$; fitting the flux below ${\sim}100\,\mathrm{TeV}$ instead requires $P_{\mathrm{CR}}/P_{\mathrm{th}}\lesssim 0.05$ and $\eta\lesssim 10$ for most sources. Other nearby Seyferts remain hard to detect individually. For $F_X\ge 10^{-11}\,\mathrm{erg}\,\mathrm{cm}^{-2}\,\mathrm{s}^{-1}$, the 2040 optimal stack is $N_{\mathrm{src}}\sim 50$--$70$ with Circinus and ${\sim}100$--$130$ without it.

Each of IceCube, Baikal-GVD, KM3NeT/ARCA, and P-ONE is assigned $1\,\mathrm{km}^{3}$; water detectors are given IceCube-like effective area but better angular resolution for $E_{\nu}\gtrsim 10\,\mathrm{TeV}$ because of the longer Cherenkov-photon scattering length.
