papers.title: Flux Variation of the Crab Pulsar Observed Using Fermi LAT and NuSTAR
papers.result: Pulsed Crab emission is not steady. The mean gamma-ray flux is $F_{\gamma}=(1.283\pm0.004)\times10^{-9}\,\mathrm{erg\,cm^{-2}\,s^{-1}}$ (0.1–100 GeV), with month-scale deviations from a few percent to $\sim20\%$, and $\Gamma_{\gamma}\approx2.17\pm0.02$ varying by up to $\sim10\%$. Linear slopes $(-2.65\pm0.94)\times10^{-12}\,\mathrm{erg\,cm^{-2}\,s^{-1}\,yr^{-1}}$ and $(-1.92\pm0.59)\times10^{-3}\,\mathrm{yr^{-1}}$ are poor descriptions ($\chi^2_{\nu}=1.9$, $p=2.6\times10^{-14}$; $\chi^2_{\nu}=2.7$, $p=6.8\times10^{-32}$). The X-ray means are $F_{\rm X}=(6.086\pm0.002)\times10^{-9}\,\mathrm{erg\,cm^{-2}\,s^{-1}}$ and $\Gamma_{\rm X}=1.80\pm0.05$, with slopes $(-7.95\pm0.69)\times10^{-11}\,\mathrm{erg\,cm^{-2}\,s^{-1}\,yr^{-1}}$ and $(+5.37\pm1.95)\times10^{-3}\,\mathrm{yr^{-1}}$. Flux and photon index are anti-correlated (brighter-when-harder), with $r_{\rm s}=-0.35$ ($p=4.0\times10^{-7}$) and $r_{\rm s}=-0.63$ ($p=5.5\times10^{-6}$). Nebular synchrotron, inverse-Compton, and total fluxes are not significantly correlated with the pulsed flux.
papers.problem: The work tests whether Crab pulsed high-energy emission is steady on timescales much longer than the rotation period, except for a smooth secular decline from pulsar aging, and how braking-index deviations could arise if $I$, $\mu$, or $\alpha$ change.
papers.method: Archival Fermi-LAT data (MJD 54710–60842, 100 MeV–100 GeV, about 17 yr, monthly integrals) and NuSTAR data (3.0–79.0 keV, about 13 yr) are phase-gated into pulsed and nebular spectra, with $1\sigma$ statistical plus systematic errors. Pulsed fits use $\mathrm{tbabs}\times\mathrm{powerlaw}$; nebular $N_{\rm H}=0.36\times10^{22}\,\mathrm{cm^{-2}}$ is fixed, $\Gamma_{\rm X}$ and normalization are tied within an epoch, and a 3% systematic uncertainty is included. Absorption uses the cited photoelectric cross sections. The braking index is $n=\Omega\ddot{\Omega}/\dot{\Omega}^{2}$, with spin parameters from the Jodrell Bank monthly ephemeris and $\ddot{\Omega}$ from adjacent $\dot{\Omega}$ differences. Magnetic-dipole spin-down power scales as $I\Omega\dot{\Omega}$.

papers.title: Two-component $γ$-Ray Structure from the CR Sources
papers.result: The baseline photon spectrum is $\frac{d\Phi_{\gamma}}{dE_{\gamma}}=\frac{d\Phi_{\pi^{0},\mathrm{re}}}{dE_{\gamma}}+\frac{d\Phi_{\mathrm{IC},\mathrm{fresh}}}{dE_{\gamma}}$. The low-energy bump is primarily $\pi^{0}$ emission from background cosmic rays compressed and reaccelerated in dense clouds, while the harder high-energy component is usually inverse Compton from freshly accelerated electrons and can instead be hadronic when the gas density is high. The neutrino flux is predicted from the gamma-ray-constrained proton spectrum and is not a fixed fraction of the total gamma-ray flux. Reported source scales include CTB 80 at $d=2\,\mathrm{kpc}$, W44 at about $20\,\mathrm{kyr}$ and $2.2\,\mathrm{kpc}$, $\gamma$ Cygni at about $7\,\mathrm{kyr}$, $1.7\,\mathrm{kpc}$ and radius about $15\,\mathrm{pc}$, W51C at about $5.5\,\mathrm{kpc}$ with atomic-hydrogen density about $30$–$160\,\mathrm{cm^{-3}}$, and 1LHAASO J1852+0050u above $100\,\mathrm{TeV}$ with molecular-cloud density about $360\,\mathrm{cm^{-3}}$. papers.title: Perturbative QCD Constraints on Hot Neutron-Star Matter
papers.result: Along fixed-$\hat{s}$ adiabats the allowed region shrinks monotonically as temperature rises. At $6\,n_{\rm sat}$, 4, 5, and 7 of 11 RMF models are excluded for $\hat{s}\le 1$, $\hat{s}=2$, and $\hat{s}=4$. The DD2/DD-MEX exit boundary runs from $(\mu_{\mathrm{B}},T)\simeq(2.16\,\mathrm{GeV},0)$ to $(1.55\,\mathrm{GeV},152\,\mathrm{MeV})$, crossing $n_{\mathrm{B}}^{c}=0.85\,\mathrm{fm^{-3}}$ at $T\simeq 125\,\mathrm{MeV}$.

The low anchor is HS(DD2) at $n_{\mathrm{B}}=0.176\,\mathrm{fm^{-3}}$ and the high anchor is scale-averaged pQCD at $n_{\mathrm{B}}=6.5\,\mathrm{fm^{-3}}$, with $\bar{\Lambda}=\sqrt{(0.722\times 4\pi T X_{\mathrm{lat}})^{2}+(2\mu_{\mathrm{B}}X/3)^{2}}$ log-uniformly averaged over $X\in[0.5,2.0]$. papers.title: Analysis Methodology of the Search for Ultrahigh Energy Neutrinos in 10.6 Years of Askaryan Radio Array Data
papers.result: With an effective livetime of $10.6$ yr ($25.9$ station-years after quality cuts), no neutrino candidate remains. The single phased-array event ($\mathrm{SNR}\sim 12$, elevation $-35^\circ$) is local A5 detector emission. Analysis efficiency is $28\%$ for a flux at current experimental upper limits. The $90\%$ CL all-flavor limit is the strongest reported at $50$–$1000\,\mathrm{EeV}$ and excludes the Muzio trans-GZK model. Analysis-level expectations are Global UL $5.3$ ($\epsilon=27.6\%$), Muzio $2.4$ ($21.8\%$), Kotera $0.4$ ($21.1\%$), $100\%$ protons $0.2$ ($25.0\%$), Fang pulsars $0.2$ ($16.7\%$), and KM3NeT $1.6$ ($13.8\%$).
papers.problem:
Whether a diffuse flux of ultrahigh-energy neutrinos, $E_
u\gtrsim 100\,\mathrm{PeV}$, including cosmogenic neutrinos from UHECR interactions with the CMB and EBL, is detectable through in-ice Askaryan radio pulses. u^2\Phi_
u\lesssim 10^{-8}\,\mathrm{GeV}\,\mathrm{cm}^{-2}\,\mathrm{s}^{-1}\,\mathrm{sr}^{-1}$.
papers.method: Five ARA stations (2013–2023) are analyzed with $10\%$ of data for background design and $90\%$ blinded. NuLeptonSim generates $E^{-1}$ neutrinos from $10^{16}$–$10^{21}\,\mathrm{eV}$ for later reweighting inside a fiducial cylinder, using Connolly cross sections and PREM; AraSim models the stations. AraProc22 calibrates waveforms and applies a $50$–$875\,\mathrm{MHz}$ bandpass. Signal strength is $\mathrm{SNR}=(V_{\mathrm{pp}}/2)/\mathrm{RMS}$. Direction uses $C_{ij}(\tau)$ with $n(z)=n_{\mathrm{ice}}-(n_{\mathrm{ice}}-n_{\mathrm{firn}})e^{-z/\Lambda}$ ($n_{\mathrm{ice}}=1.780$, $n_{\mathrm{firn}}=1.326$, $\Lambda\simeq 49.505\,\mathrm{m}$). Cuts minimize the $5\sigma$ discovery normalization at $E_0=10^{18.5}\,\mathrm{eV}$, $$\phi_0^{\mathrm{disc}}(\boldsymbol{\Sigma},\boldsymbol{\Theta})=\frac{\mathrm{FC}(n_{\mathrm{disc}}(B),B)}{\int f(E)\,\mathcal{E}(E)\,dE}.$$ Thermal separation uses impulsivity $\mathcal{I}=2\langle H\rangle-1$.

papers.result: Between the 2024 and 2025 XSPECT campaigns the source moved from a harder, fainter, more variable interval to a brighter, softer, less variable state. For $D\sim50\,\mathrm{kpc}$ and $i\sim67^{\circ}$, the 2025 normalization implies an apparent inner radius $\sim43\,\mathrm{km}$ and a corrected radius $\sim50\,\mathrm{km}$, close to an ISCO of $\sim53\,\mathrm{km}$ for $M\sim7\,M_{\odot}$ and $a_{\ast}\approx0.25$.
